CLV aggregation provides a scalar performance indicator grounded in realized outcomes, while probabilistic calibration ensures that model confidence aligns with empirical accuracy. Sealed splits enforce methodological rigor by preventing data leakage. These components together define a dual structure: one for empirical validation (CLV, calibration) and another for methodological integrity (split sealing). Failure modes include insufficient sample size in CLV reporting and missing model probabilities for calibration metrics. The system avoids simulation and fabricates no numbers, ensuring trustworthiness.
